text.p: Tropical Storm Willie has formed in the South China Sea, south of Hainan. The storm is expected to remain nearly stationary for the next day or two in the waters south of Hainan. Top winds, now near 40 mph, are expected to increase to near 70 mph during the next 48 hours. Willie will be a threat mainly to shipping, but all interests from northern Vietnam through Hainan and eastward to Hong Kong should monitor the progress of this storm system.

Typhoon Violet is expected to pass about 250 miles east of Okinawa, Japan, during the next 36 hours, on a track to the northeast. Top winds, now near 105 mph, will weaken further to near 90 mph, but Violet will still remain a strong storm and a fairly significant threat to shipping. The effects of the storm on Okinawa will be limited to rough surf, gusty winds from the northeast to north, and a few locally heavy rain squalls.

Tropical Storm Tom will threaten shipping only as it tracks northeastward from near 27n/150e to near 32n/157e during the next 48 hours in the western Pacific. Top winds, now near 70 mph, will weaken to near 45 mph by late in the period.

Tropical Depression 01C will be a moderate threat to shipping as it tracks westward well south of Hawaii the next few days. This system has top winds near 35 mph and may intensify to a tropical storm while passing south of Hawaii.
